clue.text: Plain store oddly containing unknown egg-based drink

parts.note: a prairie is a wide grassy plain of North America

indicators.note: containing says the scrambled store letters hold the unknown inside them
oddly says the letters of store are arranged in an unusual way

parts.note: Y is an unknown quantity in algebra, as are X and Z

explanation.surface: A shop on the flat lands strangely stocks some mysterious drink made from eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like a call for alternate letters of 'store', but it is an anagram signal: OSTER takes Y inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This hangover cure is a raw egg yolk swallowed whole with Worcestershire sauce and seasoning.

clue.text: In short, delivery person that is after work up street

indicators.note: after says the piece for that is comes behind the rest
in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: op is the short form of opus, a musical work
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A sentence about a courier coming along after a job on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' belongs to the definition: the answer is the informal clipped name for a mail carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Postie is a colloquial British shortening for the postman who brings letters to the door.

clue.text: Worker consuming tiny amount is expert on bodies

indicators.note: consuming says the outer word swallows the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a worker is a sterile ant, so worker gives ant
an atom is a minute quantity, as in not an atom of truth

explanation.surface: A labourer who eats a tiny portion turns out to know all about physiques.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a scientist studies the structure of the human and animal frame by dissection.

clue.text: Behave wildly, iron into track

definitions.note: here the definition leans on wildly as well: to behave without restraint

indicators.note: into says the scrambled metal word goes inside the track

parts.note: a rut is a groove or track worn in the ground

indicators.note: wildly says the letters of iron are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Behave wildly by putting a metal bar into a groove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' does double duty: it scrambles IRON to NRIO for RUT to hold, and completes the definition 'Behave wildly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To run riot is an idiom for acting without restraint, rampaging out of control.

clue.text: 1980s film teaching gunmen about technology

parts.note: teaching and educating both mean instructing

indicators.note: about says the gunmen go around the technology

parts.note: the RA, the Royal Artillery, is the British Army's gunners
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A film from the eighties about instructing armed men in computing.
explanation.walkthrough: The RA (Royal Artillery) is a regiment of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1983 movie starring Michael Caine and Julie Walters was adapted from Willy Russell's stage play.

clue.text: OK to pinch one thousand pounds? Blimey

indicators.note: to pinch means to squeeze between, so the agreement word grips the other letters

parts.note: yes and OK both express agreement
I is the Roman numeral for one
K, for kilo, is slang for a thousand, especially of money

explanation.surface: Someone is startled at being allowed to steal a grand.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise or alarm; blimey is a British interjection like gosh.

clue.text: Anything northern rejected for couple

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the dialect word is read backwards

parts.note: owt is a Northern English dialect word for anything

explanation.surface: Someone from up north turns down everything offered to a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is a pair, the number after one.

clue.text: Printed name of female below artist

indicators.note: below in a down clue puts the following pieces under the artist

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A woman's name printed beneath a painter's signature.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off copies is to produce them on a press or photocopier.

clue.text: Belgian town in European country

parts.note: Spa is the Belgian resort whose mineral springs gave all spas their name

explanation.surface: A Belgian resort lies within a nation of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian kingdom with Madrid as capital is a nation of Europe.

clue.text: Anonymous hunk now noticed partly

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A nameless handsome man is finally getting some attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Anonymous means without a known name or identity, unidentified.

clue.text: James in Iowa recreated World War II battle

indicators.note: recreated says the letters are made again in a new arrangement

parts.note: Jim is a short form of the name James

explanation.surface: A man restages a wartime battle in the American Midwest, as re-enactors do.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1945 fight for this Pacific island between US Marines and Japan is a famous wartime engagement.

clue.text: Flesh going off in storage space

indicators.note: going off means spoiling, so the letters of flesh decay into a new order

explanation.surface: Meat is rotting in the larder.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge fixed to a wall or in a cupboard is where things are stored.

clue.text: Constant look inside to make certain space fenced off

indicators.note: inside says the first pieces sit within the verb for making certain

parts.note: to ensure is to make certain
c is the symbol for the constant speed of light
lo is an old word meaning look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on things inside to be sure a fenced area is secure.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure is an area surrounded by a fence or wall, such as a paddock.

clue.text: Popular coach, when heart deficient, so essential

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the coach word loses its central letter, its heart

parts.note: to coach is to train
sic, Latin for thus or so, marks a quotation as given

explanation.surface: A well-liked trainer, lacking courage, is nonetheless vital.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrinsic means belonging to the basic nature of something, inherent and fundamental.

clue.text: Sort of cat is returned in the morning and leashed regularly

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is is read backwards

parts.note: a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before noon

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of leashed is taken

explanation.surface: A cat comes back in the morning and is put on a lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of slender cat with blue eyes and dark points, originating in Thailand.

clue.text: Mother tours Australia with extremely reticent musical composer

indicators.note: tours means travels around, so mother surrounds the country

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
Oz is a colloquial name for Australia

indicators.note: extremely says the outermost letters of reticent are taken

explanation.surface: Mum travels round Australia with a shy man of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfgang Amadeus, the Austrian prodigy behind The Magic Flute, wrote operas and symphonies.

clue.text: Section on rubbish dump, raised place for deodorant?

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the section above the dump

parts.note: an arm is a branch or section of an organisation
a pit can be a dump, as in the place is a pit

explanation.surface: Part of a landfill site is an odd spot for applying a body spray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' belongs to the definition: the limb is lifted to apply the product underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollow under the shoulder is where people apply antiperspirant, lifting the limb to do so.

clue.text: Perform better than old-fashioned party

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A dated celebration is outshone.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass someone is to exceed them in performance.

clue.text: Farm animal I'd put on drug, a chemical compound

indicators.note: put on in a down clue sets the earlier pieces above the drug

parts.note: an ox is a bovine kept on a farm
I'd without its apostrophe
E is slang for ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone would dose a farm beast with medicine, producing a chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: A binary compound of oxygen with another element, such as rust, is a chemical compound.

clue.text: Alluring beauty finally deserting old Hollywood actress

indicators.note: finally says the closing letter of deserting is taken

parts.note: Dorothy Lamour starred in the Road films with Bob Hope and Bing Crosby

explanation.surface: A beauty leaves behind a star of the old studio era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserting' looks like a deletion signal; it only gives its final letter. 'Alluring beauty' is the definition, not the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is attractive or exciting charm, the allure of the film star.

clue.text: Winged symbols appearing in diagram or in illustration

indicators.note: appearing in says the answer shows itself inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Winged figures are shown in a picture or drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorini are cherubic cupids in art, winged infants that symbolise love.

clue.text: It's used for paddling round a river

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Something for paddling around a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole with a blade, pulled through water to propel a rowing boat.

clue.text: Supply key joke

parts.note: E is a musical key
a quip is a witty remark or joke

explanation.surface: Provide a crucial gag.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to furnish or provide with what is needed.

clue.text: The vet yearned to reform equestrian contest

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An animal doctor longed to change horse-riding competitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A competition for horse and rider over consecutive days of dressage, cross-country and show jumping.
